content: Tesseract.js does not downscale large input images by default; the WebAssembly heap can grow to accommodate a large image but never shrinks back, so one oversized photo can permanently bloat memory for the life of the worker (documented GitHub issue, RAM usage reported in the 10GB+ range in pathological cases). Mitigation: resize/downscale images client-side before OCR (about 1200px width preserves legibility while cutting memory ~56% vs 4K) and use a bounded worker pool via a scheduler rather than spawning workers per request. Accuracy: Tesseract lags well behind cloud OCR engines (Google Vision, PaddleOCR) especially on noisy/angled real-world photos, so expect materially lower accuracy on live-camera captures than on clean uploaded screenshots.
